phrases.latin: corvōs, quī super agrōs crōciēbant, et cornīcēs, quārum ūna in fraxinō sedēns clāmābat
phrases.english: ravens croaking over the fields, and crows, one of which sat calling in an ash tree

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 144.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
